thesis: Lennar trades at 0.92x its own reported book value and Berkshire Hathaway bought $329,017,222 of it on the open market on 2026-10-02 at 77.12-81.90, which is 0.85-0.90x. The Q3 FY2026 release I read gives stockholders equity of $21,558,959 thousand on 237,756 thousand weighted diluted shares — $90.68 of book per share — against net homebuilding debt of $3,147,136 thousand, just 12.7% of total capital, $1.15bn of homebuilding cash and only $650m drawn on a $3.1bn revolver. That is a balance sheet built to be bored for two years, which is the only thing a 4.98% 10-year actually requires of it. The de-rating is real and so is its cause: new orders fell to 20,879 homes from 23,004 a year earlier, -9.2%. What is not justified is paying less than liquidation-adjusted equity for the second-largest US homebuilder while it still earns a 15.8% gross margin on every house it does sell.
key_risk: Four consecutive quarters have MISSED consensus (-9.2%, -1.1%, -3.9%, -13.7%) and orders are shrinking, so book value is not guaranteed to compound — a homebuilder that takes land impairments destroys the exact anchor this thesis rests on. INVALIDATION, and it is not a price move: stockholders equity per share declines in two consecutive quarters, or homebuilding gross margin on home sales prints below 14.0% (it was 15.8% in Q3 FY2026). Either would mean the book I am paying 0.92x for is being written down rather than waited out, and the position should be closed regardless of price. Note also that I am recommending CLOSING BCC today out of the same housing complex; the distinction is deliberate and is in the counter_argument.
counter_argument: The strongest case against is that every housing asset is the same bet and I am closing one today: BCC goes out at a new 120-day low out of the same end-market. The distinction is the balance sheet and what each company owns. BCC sells commodity OSB and plywood at a spot price it does not set, has no book-value floor to buy below, and shows deteriorating analyst revisions, a -7.7% miss and zero insider buying; LEN owns a land bank carried at cost with 12.7% net leverage and has the largest open-market buyer in American finance under it at 0.85x book. The second objection is better: Berkshire is early as often as it is right, bought six weeks ago, and is barely above water at 83.58 — which is precisely why the entry is an accumulation in thirds down to 77.50 rather than a single purchase at the market, and why the invalidation is written on book value rather than on the share price.

thesis: On 2026-08-25 DKS fell 30.7% in a day (179.33 to 124.31), its worst session on record, when FY2026 adjusted EPS guidance was cut to $11-12 from $13.50-14.50. The cut was not the core business: the DICKS banner comped +4.9% while the acquired Foot Locker unit comped -3.6% and swung from a guided $110-150m operating PROFIT to a guided $40-80m operating LOSS. That is a fixable inventory and promotion problem inside an acquisition, not a broken retailer, and management has reiterated $100-125m of cost synergies. Seven distinct insiders then bought $5.59m on the open market at 129.75-136.39 in September with no offsetting cluster of sales, and the tape has begun to agree: +7.97pp against SPY over one month after -25.4pp over three, now above a rising SMA20 143.82 and SMA50 137.43 with the 2026-11-12 pullback coming on the lightest volume of twenty sessions.
key_risk: The last two quarters MISSED (-7.1% on 2026-09-30, -1.0% on 2026-06-30) and a third miss on 2026-11-23 — or any further cut to the $11-12 range — takes the stock through the 135.02/135.29 twin lows. The stop at 132.25 is 2.03 ATR away on a name with a 4.13% daily range and a demonstrated capacity to fall 30% in one session, so it will be gapped through, not touched: the real risk on this idea is the full 12.25 and possibly more, and 2.5% is sized for that. The thesis also rests on secondary coverage of the August guidance cut rather than on a filing I read.
counter_argument: The strongest case against is that the multiple never actually compressed, so there is no cheapness to collect. That is correct and it is the right way to read it: 179.33 before the cut was 12.81x the old $14.00 EPS midpoint, and 145.66 today is 12.67x the new $11.50 midpoint — the entire 40% drawdown is the earnings cut, not a de-rating. So this cannot be a multiple re-rating trade and is not pitched as one; it is a bet that $11-12 is the trough. The second objection is the sell side, which is capitulating rather than accumulating: bullish share 61.3% to 53.1%, holds 11 to 13, two outright sells — the weakest configuration of any name screened today.
